clue.text: Relative support for advancement

blocks.note: surface reading: comparative help given to someone trying to get ahead
setter's reading: backing given to one's relatives, so that family members get promoted

explanation.surface: How much help someone gets in climbing the career ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative' looks like an adjective meaning comparative, but it is a noun: a family member being favoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is the practice of those in power favouring kin, especially by giving them jobs.

clue.text: Striking tone upset important person

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a worthy is a notable, distinguished person

explanation.surface: A dignitary was rattled by a remarkable tone of voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking is remarkable enough to deserve notice, which is what noteworthy says.

clue.text: Rag committee are involved with packaging

blocks.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper, a paper
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: Students organising a charity rag week get tangled up in packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: A student rag is a British university charity event, which the surface suggests; in the wordplay a rag is a low-grade newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Paperboard is the thick card used to make boxes and cartons, so it serves as packaging material.

clue.text: Rigid first to last in squabbles

indicators.note: this tells us to move the opening letter of the word round to its end

blocks.note: rigid and stiff are synonyms

explanation.surface: Someone inflexible from start to finish whenever an argument breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffs are petty quarrels, the same thing as squabbles.

clue.text: Best back number's in colour

indicators.note: one item sits in another, so it is placed inside the word for colour

blocks.note: to back a motion is to second it
NO is the standard abbreviation for number
a tone is a shade or colour

explanation.surface: The best way to present a reversed number is in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the verb meaning support, as when a motion is seconded at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Second to none is an idiom for unbeaten by anything, that is, the best.

clue.text: It's bad to aim insult

blocks.note: food that has gone bad is said to be off
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Setting out to cause insult is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend someone is to give them insult, hurting their feelings.

clue.text: Base insecure, having no ties

blocks.note: the foot of something is its base
something loose is not secure

explanation.surface: A shaky foundation, with nothing holding it down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone footloose is free to travel or act as they please, without commitments.

clue.text: Get paid, being keen but not established

indicators.note: but not says the word that follows must be taken away from what came before

blocks.note: earnest means serious and eager, keen
EST is the abbreviation for established, as on shop signs

explanation.surface: A newcomer who is keen but has no track record still gets wages.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to receive money in return for work, that is, to get paid.

clue.text: Up and down action

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading up and down gives the same word, so it must read identically both ways

blocks.note: an act, which reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Plenty of activity, rising and falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up and down' sounds like a description of movement, but it tells you the four letters read the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is something done, an act or action.

clue.text: Sort to confront a particular group of characters

blocks.note: a sort is a kind or type
to face someone is to confront them

explanation.surface: Arranging a showdown with a certain gang of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' suggests people, but the definition means printed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface is one design of printed letters, a set of characters sharing one style.

clue.text: Recce round building for bully

indicators.note: building means constructing something, so the letters are assembled into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written; a recce is military slang for a reconnaissance
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A scouting trip around a building on the lookout for a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce is to force someone by threats, which is to bully them.

clue.text: Unemotional material and bad performance

blocks.note: matter is physical material or substance
milk that is bad has gone off
an act is a turn or performance on stage

explanation.surface: A critic coldly lists the stuff of a poor show.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter-of-fact manner is plain and practical, showing no feeling.

clue.text: Rough was darn tall, though nothing's concealed

indicators.note: rough means crude or unpolished, so the following words are roughly rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rugged, very tall figure who hides nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from Cromwell asking to be painted with every blemish shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Warts and all means including every flaw, with no attempt to hide imperfections.

clue.text: Loud and burliest one, possibly, to speak at length against the law

definitions.text: to speak at length against the law

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters before it are reordered

blocks.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A loud, hefty politician talks on and on to block a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: In legislatures such as the US Senate a filibuster is a marathon speech meant to delay a vote on a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To filibuster is to make a very long speech so as to obstruct passage of a law.

clue.text: Heartless Lucy and Ethel are confused, spiritually

indicators.note: without a heart, the name keeps only its outside letters
confused means muddled up, so the gathered letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two friends, one cold-hearted, are bewildered in a spiritual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means heavenly or unworldly, so ethereally is in a spiritual, otherworldly manner.

clue.text: Castles in the air?

blocks.note: surface reading: the idiom for daydreams and fanciful plans
setter's reading: the chess pieces called castles share their other name with crows that fly in the air

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom castles in the air means impossible dreams; here the chess castle, also called by a bird's name, is literally airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooks are both the chess pieces also called castles and black crows that nest in colonies.

clue.text: Only my tin used for collection, which is something serious

indicators.note: a collection gathers things together any old how, so the letters are regathered in a new order

blocks.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A charity collector rattles only their own tin, a grave matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemnity is seriousness and gravity, or a formal ceremonial occasion.

clue.text: One concerned to make his mark seen to toast it badly

definitions.text: One concerned to make his mark

indicators.note: badly done means botched, so the preceding words come out rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An ambitious person seen making a clumsy toast at a dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make his mark' sounds like ambition, but this person literally marks skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist's job is inking permanent designs into people's skin, quite literally making marks.

clue.text: Not easy to go by ship for one who's uncompromising

blocks.note: hard means difficult, not easy
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Travelling by sea is tough for someone who never gives ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardliner holds rigidly to a policy or position and refuses to compromise.

clue.text: Pick the best

blocks.note: first meaning: the pick of a group, its choicest members
second meaning: the top people in a field

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to choose the best, but 'Pick' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the select top members of a group, both the pick of the bunch and the best.

clue.text: Football club split, forfeiting right in the process

indicators.note: to forfeit something is to lose it, so a letter for the next word is dropped

blocks.note: Man U is the common short name of Manchester United
a fracture is a split or break
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A football club divided, losing its right to something along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester United is an English football club, often called Man U.
explanation.definitionFit: Manufacture is the process of making goods on a large scale.

clue.text: Simple English used in the family

indicators.note: something used in another thing goes inside it, so the letter is placed within

blocks.note: a clan is an extended family
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Plain English is what's spoken at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean can mean simple and uncluttered, as in clean lines of a design.

clue.text: Concrete business

blocks.note: first meaning: solid and definite, as in a concrete offer
second meaning: a company

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a building-trade company, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means solid or definite as an adjective, and a commercial company as a noun.

clue.text: Knocks up box

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: raps are sharp knocks

explanation.surface: Someone bangs together a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocks up' reads as the phrasal verb for making something hastily; split it into knocks plus a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice.

clue.text: Rascal to disclose damage

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a rascal
to air views is to make them public

explanation.surface: A scamp is about to spill the secret and do harm.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or damage it.

clue.text: Concerning those with an issue for reformed art panel

indicators.note: reformed means made into a new shape, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People with a complaint about a reorganised arts committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a grievance, but it is the formal word for children, offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Parental means relating to parents, who are those with issue, that is, offspring.

clue.text: One exaggerating distress caused by damage to most of feature on car

indicators.note: most of means not all, so the last letter of the next word is cut

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
a tyre is a feature of a car's wheel, spelt the British way

explanation.surface: Someone overdoing their upset after a scrape to their car.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a martyr informally means they make a great show of their suffering to gain sympathy.

clue.text: Fish straying at sea?

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and adrift, so the word is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish wandering off in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat sea fish with a venomous spine on its tail.
